keyFindings.title: **Defer/negative/holdout counting — the retired semantics give a defensible rule.** (a) `stage: negative` / `expected_workflow_mode: UNKNOWN` / rejection labels `none|defer|unknown` → expected set is empty: compiled MUST NOT route; a route is unsafe over-detection and blocks. (b) `routeOutcome: defer` gold → compiled `action` must be non-route; routing is drift. (c) Routing-stage scenarios where gold routes → compiled `defer` is a silent defer and blocks. (d) `stage: holdout` counts identically to routing — holdout is keyword-blind anti-overfit evidence, not a discount tier. (e) `classKind: browser` and gold-absent rows stay `n/a`, out of the denominator. These are exactly the Section-4 bar's own terms: "zero drift, zero unsafe over-detection, zero silent defers on a scenario legacy actually routes." keyFindings.title: **Gold-checking measures something deliberately different from parity — stricter in one axis, looser in another.** Parity required `compiled == legacy` regardless of gold achievability (a shared pre-existing gold gap was parity, not drift). A gold checker requires `compiled == gold`: (a) it FAILS a hub where compiled==legacy but both miss authored gold — e.g. the documented CS-002/CS-005 "non-Webflow" negation quirk where both engines shared the same gold gap and parity held at 0 drift; (b) it PASSES a hub where compiled is correct-but-different-from-legacy — meaning serving could change behavior on scenarios gold doesn't cover, where parity guaranteed zero behavior change. Which semantic the bar should mean is an admission-policy decision, not a technical one. Lane C parity compared the live compiled decision (public front door, SPECKIT_COMPILED_ROUTING=1) against the Mode A legacy replay per playbook scenario, with three honesty guards and five statuses.
A restore needs four deleted modules (845+1889+741+766 lines), their test, a driver, the corpus and shared deps; the three frozen scorer files are SHA-256-pinned, so any edit forces re-pinning.
The retirement was deliberate and broad (BREAKING CHANGE; five entry points, script tree, fixtures, typed ledgers removed), and the spec fences off reopening the lane as a whole.
The live typed-gold corpus is 74 scenarios across the five admitted hubs (64 concrete, 2 defer, 8 UNKNOWN) plus 19 holdout and 2 negative; sk-code contributes only 1 scenario.

compiledRoute returns qualified-id targets only; checking leaf gold requires the live qualifiedIdToLeaf bridge over each hub's leaf-manifest + mode-registry, and the result is mode-granular must-include, not legacy's task-scoped assembly.
Compiled action vocabulary (route/clarify/defer/reject; canary histogram 50/3/7/7) exceeds the gold vocabulary, so a new checker must define the non-route mapping itself.

Defer must count as a no-route assertion (over-detection and silent-default both fail); holdout counts in the verdict with the fitted-vs-holdout gap reported; negative scenarios are suppression assertions; UNKNOWN maps to the empty expected-intent set.

A gold-only checker has one observation: it is stricter against gold but blind to legacy drift, so the admission sentence changes from 'compiled equals legacy' to 'compiled satisfies the authored routing contract'.
Eight cohort surfaces must change for an eighth hub; four lockstep copies are test-guarded, guard/sync/closure are not, and the cohort length is asserted by expect(cohort.length).toBe(5).

mint writes an inert legacy/shadowOnly manifest and refuses to overwrite; refresh increments generation and preserves servingAuthority/shadowOnly; freshness must compare against the hub's own shadow-child snapshot; no CLI flips authority to compiled.

Freshness is enforced at three moments: pre-commit auto re-mint (SKILL.md trigger, staged+unstaged refusal, authored-copy sync), compiled-route-guard.cjs (stale-manifest + authored-drift + narrow exemptions), and the request-time status probe (causeCode matrix).
compiled-route-sync traces require/file reads across every hub to promote the closure (48 files); a new hub's shadow child must join the traced path and the sync HUBS list or it is never promoted.

The cohort history is 7 (all hubs) -> 6 (sk-design dissolution, phase 023) -> 5 (sk-prompt retirement 8da89c0594e); the architecture reference still says seven hubs and names the legacy layout paths (006/011/010), while the live layout is 009/014/013.
A post-retirement manual playbook-verify (resolve.cjs vs router-replay.cjs, diffed per scenario) was already used for sk-prompt and recorded 5/5, 0 drift, but left no reusable tool.

Costs: Path A = 4,241 lines + test + driver + frozen pins + retired-lane drag; Path B = low hundreds of lines, no frozen parts, standing-gate capable; Path C = zero build, permanent manual admission, no compiled-vs-legacy measurement.

No standing gate compares compiled to legacy since retirement: CI covers structure, freshness and 2 golden prompts with expectedMode; canary fixtures are evaluated only when the generator runs, and loadSnapshot does not evaluate them.

Recommendation: Path B as a standing gate with the bar restated; six build steps; the operator's single decision is accepting the restated sentence or demanding literal legacy equality (decided with the baseline report).
